title: Toxic Memes: A Survey of Computational Perspectives on the Detection and Explanation of Meme Toxicities

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting misogyny, sexism, and gender-based stereotyping in multimodal memes.
Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting racism, white supremacist extremism, and hate speech targeting racial groups in memes.
Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting religious hate speech, including Islamophobia and antisemitism, in memes.
Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting ableism and hate speech targeting individuals with disabilities in memes.
Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting homophobia and hate speech targeting sexual orientation in memes.
Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting political propaganda and mitigating unintended political bias in meme detection systems.
Evaluation of the linguistic diversity of existing meme datasets, identifying a significant overrepresentation of English and a lack of resources for low-resource languages.
Systematic survey of datasets and computational models focused on detecting xenophobia and hate speech based on nationality or immigration status in memes.
